body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}((p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha})\ge1-\alpha/3\). On this event, \(\max_x|p_x-\widehat p_x|\le[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\); moreover \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(\min_xn_x<np_{\min}/2)\le|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). Put \(e_{p,n}=[\log(6|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/(2n)]^{1/2}\). If \(p=(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) and \(p'=(p'_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), while \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) are fixed for every \(x\), then \[\sup_{a\in I}\left|\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|\le2|\mathcal X|\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n},\] and the right-hand side is \(o(r_n)\).
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m=|\mathcal X|\) and
\[
 e_{p,n}=\left\{\frac{\log(6m/\alpha)}{2n}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
We first prove the concentration statement.  If \(Z\in[0,1]\) and \(\psi(\lambda)=\log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\), exponential tilting gives \(\psi''(\lambda)=\operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)\).  Every tilted law remains supported on \([0,1]\), so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\lambda}(Z)
 \le E_{\lambda}\{(Z-1/2)^2\}\le\frac14.
\]
Together with \(\psi(0)=\psi'(0)=0\), two integrations yield
\[
 \log E\exp\{\lambda(Z-EZ)\}\le\frac{\lambda^2}{8},
 \qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R.                                    \tag{1}
\]
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid}\) makes \(\widehat p_x\) the average of \(n\) independent Bernoulli variables with common mean \(p_x\).  Exponential Markov inequality, (1), and optimization give
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \bigl(|\widehat p_x-p_x|>e_{p,n}\bigr)
 \le2e^{-2ne_{p,n}^2}=\frac{\alpha}{3m}.                          \tag{2}
\]
The union bound over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) therefore gives
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\max_{x\in\mathcal X}|\widehat p_x-p_x|\le e_{p,n}\right)
 \ge1-\frac\alpha3.                                               \tag{3}
\]
The true mass vector is nonnegative and sums to one.  Hence, by \(\mathrm{def{:}mass\text{-}confidence\text{-}region}\), the event in (3) is exactly \(\{(p_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\in\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\}\), and the asserted coordinate bound is part of the same definition.

For the cell-count assertion, let \(N\) be binomial with parameters \(n\) and \(p\).  For \(t>0\), exponential Markov inequality and \(1-p+pe^{-t}\le\exp\{p(e^{-t}-1)\}\) imply
\[
 \Pr(N\le np/2)
 \le\exp\{tnp/2+np(e^{-t}-1)\}.
\]
Taking \(t=\log2\) makes the exponent \(-np(1-\log2)/2\le-np/8\).  Since \(n_x\) is binomial with parameters \(n\) and \(p_x\), assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strata}\) and a union bound give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}
 \left(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}n_x<np_{\min}/2\right)
 &\le\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}(n_x<np_x/2)\\
 &\le m e^{-np_{\min}/8}.                                       \tag{4}
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to bound mass profiling.  Let \(p=(p_x)\) and \(p'=(p'_x)\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{n,\alpha}\), and fix \(f_x\in\mathscr F_n\) and \(q_x\in\mathscr Q_n(f_x)\) in every cell.  Put \(e_n=a_{q,n}+B_Ya_{f,n}\).  The continuum constraints in \(\mathrm{def{:}signal\text{-}sieves}\) give, for \(a\in I\),
\[
 f_x(a)\ge\kappa/2,
 \qquad |q_x(a)|\le B_Yf_x(a)+e_n.
\]
The denominator is therefore strictly positive, and \(b_{\mu,n}=4e_n/\kappa\) gives
\[
 \left|\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}\right|
 \le B_Y+\frac{2e_n}{\kappa}
 =B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2.                                         \tag{5}
\]
Both mass vectors are within \(e_{p,n}\) of \(\widehat p\) coordinatewise.  Thus (5) and the triangle inequality imply
\[
 \sup_{a\in I}\left|
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}(p_x-p'_x)\frac{q_x(a)}{f_x(a)}
 \right|
 \le2m\left(B_Y+\frac{b_{\mu,n}}2\right)e_{p,n}.                \tag{6}
\]
Finally put \(\gamma=\beta-1/2>0\).  The tuning definitions in \(\mathrm{def{:}upper\text{-}tuning\text{-}grid}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}ecf\text{-}radii}\) give
\[
 K_n\sim\frac{\log n}{\log\log n},\qquad
 b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{-\gamma})=O(r_n).
\]
Since \(m,\alpha,B_Y\), and all class radii are fixed,
\[
 \log\left(\frac{e_{p,n}}{r_n}\right)
 =-\frac12\log n+\gamma\log\!\left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)+O(1)
 \longrightarrow-\infty.                                        \tag{7}
\]
Also \(b_{\mu,n}=o(1)\).  Equations (6)--(7) therefore show that its right-hand side is \(o(r_n)\).  This uses exactly \(\gamma>0\), equivalently \(\beta>1/2\), and proves the claim throughout the enlarged smoothness range.
body.justification: The empirical cell masses are random inputs to the causal mixture and must enter the same simultaneous coverage event as the two transform channels.
body.gap: The blind-deconvolution comparators do not profile finite-stratum causal weights jointly with probability and marked transform restrictions.
body.consumer: The bound adds cell-count uncertainty to coverage and records that mass uncertainty would be negligible at the candidate scale \(r_n\); it does not assert a shrinking total band diameter.
